title: 哈雷彗星今晚砸地球
title_en: Halley's Comet Is Hitting Us Tonight

segments.zh: Tonight, tiny pieces of Halley's Comet are slamming into Earth.
segments.en: 今晚，哈雷彗星的碎片正在砸向地球。

segments.zh: At 66 kilometers per second.
That's about 150,000 miles an hour.
And you can watch it from your backyard.
segments.en: 而你在自家后院就能看。

segments.zh: It's the Orionid meteor shower,
peaking right about now.
Today's question: how does a speck smaller than a grain of sand
segments.en: 今天的问题：一粒比沙子还小的灰，

segments.zh: light up the whole sky?
segments.en: 怎么能把整片天空点亮？

segments.zh: Meet Dusty.
Dusty is a crumb of Halley's Comet.
segments.en: 小尘是哈雷彗星掉下来的一点渣。

segments.zh: Halley's Comet swings by the Sun
about every 76 years.
Each time, the Sun cooks it,
and it sheds dust like a dog sheds fur.
Over thousands of orbits,
that dust spreads into a long, dirty ring.
segments.en: 这些灰铺成了一条长长的脏带子。

segments.zh: Every October, Earth drives right through it.
segments.en: 每年十月，地球正好从里面穿过。

segments.zh: Same time, every year.
Like driving through a cloud of bugs
on the highway.
Twist one: we hit it head-on.
segments.en: 反转一：我们是迎头撞上的。

segments.zh: Halley orbits the Sun the opposite way to us.
segments.en: 哈雷彗星绕太阳的方向跟地球相反。

segments.zh: So the speeds add up.
Head-on collisions are the worst kind.
66 kilometers per second
is roughly 70 times faster than a rifle bullet.
And energy grows with speed squared.
segments.en: 而能量跟速度的平方走。

segments.zh: Double the speed, four times the punch.
Our rough estimate: a one-milligram speck at that speed
segments.en: 我们估算一下：1毫克的小灰，这个速度，

segments.zh: carries about 2,000 joules.
segments.en: 带着大约两千焦耳的能量。

segments.zh: That's more energy
segments.en: 这比一颗手枪子弹的能量

segments.zh: than a pistol bullet.
Twist two: it's not friction
that makes it glow.
Dusty is so fast, the air can't get out of the way.
segments.en: 小尘太快了，空气来不及让开，

segments.zh: It piles up in front, squeezed and scorching hot.
segments.en: 在它前面挤成一堆，又烫又密。

segments.zh: Squeeze air hard enough and fast enough,
and it heats to thousands of degrees.
Like a bike pump getting hot,
but on fast-forward.
Dusty boils away, atom by atom,
segments.en: 小尘一个原子一个原子地蒸发掉，

segments.zh: more than 100 kilometers up.
segments.en: 大约在一百多公里的高空。

segments.zh: Those hot atoms, and the air around them, glow.
segments.en: 这些滚烫的原子和周围的空气在发光，

segments.zh: Like a neon sign.
So the streak you see is not a rock on fire.
segments.en: 所以你看到的那道光，不是一块烧着的石头，

segments.zh: It's a tube of glowing air, kilometers long.
segments.en: 而是一条几公里长、发光的空气管子。

segments.zh: Twist three, the weird part:
the streak is way bigger than Dusty.
segments.en: 那道光比小尘大太多了。

segments.zh: A crumb you could lose on your fingertip
segments.en: 放在指尖上都找不到的一点渣，

segments.zh: makes a line you can see from 100 kilometers away.
segments.en: 能划出一百公里外都看得见的线。

segments.zh: About half the Orionids even leave glowing trails
segments.en: 大约一半的猎户座流星，还会留下发光的尾迹，

segments.zh: that hang in the sky for a moment.
And none of them reach the ground.
segments.en: 而且它们一个都落不到地上。

segments.zh: Dusty is gone long before it gets close.
How to watch: go out in the dark hours before dawn
segments.en: 怎么看：天亮前那几个小时，

segments.zh: and get away from city lights.
The Moon sets around 2 a.m.,
segments.en: 月亮大约凌晨两点落下，

segments.zh: so the sky gets darker after that.
Look anywhere in the sky.
The streaks all seem to fly out of Orion.
segments.en: 流星都像是从猎户座里飞出来的。

segments.zh: Give your eyes 20 minutes.
And put your phone away.
Friendly fine print: maybe 15 to 20 an hour at best,
segments.en: 友情提示：最好的时候，一小时也就15到20颗，

segments.zh: so bring patience and a blanket.
Missed it? Halley's dust comes back every October.
segments.en: 错过了？哈雷的灰每年十月都会回来。

segments.zh: And Halley itself returns in 2061.
Dusty waited thousands of years for this moment.
segments.en: 小尘等了几千年，就为这一刻。

segments.zh: It lasted one second, and it was glorious.
segments.en: 只亮了一秒，可是真灿烂。

elements.text: air can't move out of the way
